terms.meaning: a rule that gives exactly one output for each allowed input
the set of inputs a function accepts
the set of all outputs a function can produce
a domain deliberately limited, e.g. x ≥ 0, often to make a function one-to-one
a function where different inputs can give the same output, like x² (2 and −2 both give 4)
a function where different inputs always give different outputs, like 2x + 3
a graph is a function if no vertical line crosses it more than once
a function defined by different formulas on different parts of its domain
one function applied to the output of another, written f(g(x)), fg(x) or (f∘g)(x)
f⁻¹, the function that reverses f: if f(3) = 9 then f⁻¹(9) = 3

symbols.meaning: the input on the left is turned into the output on the right
the output of function f when the input is x
the composite function f(g(x)): g first, then f

formulas.latex: f(a)=\text{the rule with every }x\text{ replaced by }(a)
